title: Token Shear and Proportional Gap Constraints for Responsive Tables & Charts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our component library contains multiple ad-hoc spacing and elevation tokens used by tables and chart overlays. This causes inconsistent density across breakpoints, visual jitter during transitions, and non-deterministic z-ordering that complicates QA and increases CSS size.

Goal: Replace the scattered tokens with a constrained set of 'shear-aware' spacing tokens and a proportional gap system that scales predictably across breakpoints and content density. Refine shadow/elevation tokens into a compact palette optimized for raster and GPU compositing (fewer layers, predictable alpha). Update typography scale pairs used inside dense table cells and chart labels to preserve legibility while minimizing line-height bloat.

Scope:
- Define 6 shear-aware spacing tokens (s-shear-0 .. s-shear-5) with proportional relationships for horizontal/vertical deltas used by Tables and Charts.
- Introduce 'gap-ratio' token family to express proportional gaps (e.g., gap-ratio-0.5, gap-ratio-1, gap-ratio-1.5) that components can multiply against base spacing.
- Consolidate radius tokens for compact controls used in tables (compact-card-radius, chip-radius) with clear migration rules.
- Rework elevation tokens into 4 composite layers (elev-flat, elev-soft, elev-pop, elev-peak) with CSS variables tuned for GPU-friendly box-shadow and fallback for older browsers.
- Adjust typography scale for dense rows: create dense-type-12/13/14 with tightened letter-spacing and controlled line-height.

Why this approach: The shear-aware and proportional-gap concepts let tables and chart overlays maintain consistent perceived density when the container or content shears (e.g., ephemerally wider labels, pinned columns). Composite elevation reduces repaints and encourages using single-layer shadow tokens in performance-critical lists.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change global color palettes beyond minor contrast tweaks for dense labels, and it does not alter interactive motion tokens (those are tracked in DES-78100).
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens defined with token names and CSS variable examples in Figma and Confluence
Migration guide added with mapping table from legacy tokens to new tokens
Design review approval from PM and Eng (recorded in comments)
GitHub PR with tokens and component updates merged and smoke-tested on staging
Accessibility report showing no regressions in contrast and reduced overlap for dense tables
Performance benchmarks showing reduced paint cost for large table renders (>=10% improvement in paint time)
